nodes.description: The quantity H(α) = −Σ μ(Aᵢ) log μ(Aᵢ) measuring the information content of a measurable partition α.

nodes.name: Pesin stable/unstable manifold theorem
nodes.description: For a C^{1+α} diffeomorphism preserving a hyperbolic measure, almost every point admits smooth local stable and unstable manifolds tangent to the Oseledets subspaces.

nodes.name: Arnold diffusion
nodes.description: The phenomenon in Hamiltonian systems with three or more degrees of freedom where orbits drift along resonances through gaps between KAM tori.

nodes.name: Nekhoroshev theorem
nodes.description: For a steep (or convex) nearly integrable Hamiltonian, action variables remain close to their initial values for exponentially long times in 1/ε.

nodes.name: Pitchfork bifurcation
nodes.description: A local bifurcation in which a symmetric equilibrium loses stability and two new equilibria appear (supercritical) or an unstable pair merges (subcritical).

nodes.name: Birkhoff normal form
nodes.type_signature: (Hamiltonian near elliptic equilibrium) → (integrable truncation in action-angle-like variables up to finite order)
nodes.description: A canonical near-identity transformation that reduces a Hamiltonian near an elliptic fixed point to a function of action variables alone up to a prescribed order.

nodes.name: Rössler attractor
nodes.description: A chaotic attractor of a three-dimensional ODE system with a single quadratic nonlinearity exhibiting a folded-band structure.

nodes.name: Benedicks–Carleson theorem
nodes.description: For a positive-measure set of parameters near a = 2, the quadratic map x ↦ 1 − ax² has an absolutely continuous invariant measure and a positive Lyapunov exponent.

nodes.name: Thermodynamic formalism
nodes.type_signature: (Dynamical system, potential φ) → (equilibrium states, pressure, Gibbs measures)
nodes.description: A framework adapting statistical mechanics (pressure, partition functions, Gibbs measures) to study invariant measures and entropy of dynamical systems.

nodes.name: Ruelle–Perron–Frobenius theorem
nodes.description: For an expanding or hyperbolic system with a Hölder potential, the transfer operator has a simple maximal eigenvalue whose eigenfunction determines the unique equilibrium state.

nodes.name: Domain of holomorphy
nodes.description: An open set in ℂⁿ that is the maximal domain of existence of some holomorphic function, equivalently a pseudoconvex domain.

nodes.name: Holomorphically convex domain
nodes.description: An open set Ω ⊂ ℂⁿ such that for every compact K ⊂ Ω the holomorphically convex hull K̂_Ω is again compact in Ω.

nodes.name: Plurisubharmonic function
nodes.description: An upper semicontinuous function φ: Ω → [−∞,∞) whose restriction to every complex line is subharmonic, the fundamental convexity notion in several complex variables.

nodes.name: Levi problem (solution)
nodes.description: A domain in ℂⁿ is a domain of holomorphy if and only if it is pseudoconvex, solved by Oka, Bremermann, and Norguet.

nodes.name: Cousin problem
nodes.description: The additive (Cousin I) and multiplicative (Cousin II) problems of constructing global meromorphic functions from local data, generalizing Mittag-Leffler and Weierstrass to several variables.

nodes.name: Oka–Cartan theorem
nodes.description: On a Stein manifold, every coherent analytic sheaf is acyclic and globally generated (Cartan's Theorems A and B for Stein manifolds).

nodes.name: Grauert direct image theorem
nodes.description: The higher direct images of a coherent analytic sheaf under a proper holomorphic map are coherent.

nodes.name: Remmert proper mapping theorem
nodes.description: The image of an analytic set under a proper holomorphic map is again an analytic set.

nodes.name: Bergman kernel
nodes.description: The reproducing kernel K(z,w) of the Hilbert space of square-integrable holomorphic functions on a bounded domain, encoding its biholomorphic geometry.

nodes.name: Szegő kernel
nodes.description: The reproducing kernel of the Hardy space H²(∂Ω) on the boundary of a domain, projecting L² boundary data onto boundary values of holomorphic functions.

nodes.name: Fefferman mapping theorem
nodes.description: A biholomorphism between smooth strictly pseudoconvex bounded domains in ℂⁿ extends to a smooth diffeomorphism of the closures.

nodes.name: Tangential Cauchy–Riemann equation
nodes.description: The system ∂̄_b u = f on a CR manifold, obtained by restricting the Cauchy–Riemann equations to the tangential directions of a real hypersurface.

nodes.name: Baouendi–Trèves approximation theorem
nodes.description: CR functions on a CR manifold can be locally uniformly approximated by restrictions of holomorphic functions from ambient space.

nodes.name: Bochner–Martinelli kernel
nodes.description: The explicit integral kernel in ℂⁿ generalizing the Cauchy kernel, used to represent holomorphic functions and solve ∂̄ in convex domains.

nodes.name: Henkin–Ramirez integral representation
nodes.type_signature: (∂̄-closed (0,q)-form on strictly pseudoconvex domain) → (explicit solution via barrier-function kernels)
nodes.description: An integral formula using holomorphic support functions that provides explicit solutions to ∂̄ with optimal Hölder estimates on strictly pseudoconvex domains.

nodes.name: Koppelman formula
nodes.description: An integral representation formula for (0,q)-forms in ℂⁿ that simultaneously generalizes Bochner–Martinelli and provides homotopy operators for ∂̄.

nodes.name: Kohn Laplacian □_b
nodes.description: The second-order operator □_b = ∂̄_b ∂̄_b* + ∂̄_b* ∂̄_b on a CR manifold, whose regularity theory underlies solvability of the tangential Cauchy–Riemann equations.

nodes.name: Edge-of-the-wedge theorem
nodes.description: If two holomorphic functions defined in wedge-shaped domains on opposite sides of a real hyperplane agree on the common edge, they extend to a single holomorphic function in a neighborhood.

nodes.name: Analytic sheaf
nodes.description: A sheaf of modules over the sheaf of germs of holomorphic functions on a complex analytic space, foundational to the Oka–Cartan theory.

nodes.name: Pluripotential theory
nodes.description: The study of plurisubharmonic functions and the complex Monge–Ampère operator (dd^c)ⁿ as a nonlinear potential theory in several complex variables.

nodes.name: Proper holomorphic mapping theorem
nodes.description: A proper holomorphic map between bounded domains is a finite branched covering, and between equidimensional balls it is an automorphism (Alexander's theorem).

nodes.name: Oka principle
nodes.description: On a Stein manifold, the inclusion of holomorphic sections into continuous sections of an elliptic submersion is a weak homotopy equivalence.

nodes.name: Weierstrass preparation theorem (several variables)
nodes.description: A holomorphic function vanishing to order k in one variable can be uniquely factored near the origin as a unit times a Weierstrass polynomial of degree k.

nodes.name: Fiber product of schemes
nodes.description: The categorical pullback X ×_S Y in the category of schemes, representing the functor of pairs of compatible morphisms, fundamental to base change.

nodes.name: Smooth morphism
nodes.description: A morphism of schemes that is flat, locally of finite presentation, and has geometrically regular fibers, generalizing submersion to algebraic geometry.

nodes.name: Verdier duality
nodes.description: A duality in the derived category of sheaves on a locally compact space giving an adjunction between f_! and f^! functors, generalizing Poincaré and Serre duality.

nodes.name: Perverse sheaf
nodes.description: An object of the heart of the perverse t-structure on the bounded derived category of constructible sheaves, satisfying support and cosupport conditions.

nodes.name: BBD decomposition theorem
nodes.description: The direct image of an intersection cohomology complex under a proper map decomposes as a direct sum of shifted semisimple perverse sheaves (Beilinson–Bernstein–Deligne).

nodes.name: Mixed Hodge structure
nodes.description: A finitely generated abelian group with an increasing weight filtration over ℚ and a decreasing Hodge filtration over ℂ satisfying compatibility conditions, present on the cohomology of all complex algebraic varieties.

nodes.name: Higher algebraic K-theory (Quillen)
nodes.description: The higher K-groups Kₙ(R) for n ≥ 0 defined via Quillen's Q-construction or +-construction on the classifying space of the category of projective modules.

nodes.name: Flip (algebraic geometry)
nodes.description: A birational surgery in the minimal model program replacing a small extremal contraction by its flip, increasing the intersection with the canonical divisor.

nodes.name: Abundance conjecture
nodes.description: On a minimal projective variety with nef canonical divisor, the canonical divisor is semiample, i.e., some multiple is base-point free.

nodes.name: Zariski decomposition
nodes.description: A pseudo-effective divisor on a smooth surface decomposes uniquely as D = P + N where P is nef and N is an effective ℚ-divisor with negative-definite intersection matrix.

nodes.name: Bloch higher Chow group
nodes.description: The group CH^p(X, n) defined as the homology of a complex of algebraic cycles on X × Δⁿ, providing a cycle-theoretic model for motivic cohomology.

nodes.name: Quillen Q-construction
nodes.description: A categorical construction that produces the algebraic K-theory space BQC from an exact category C by adding extra morphisms encoding short exact sequences.

nodes.name: Riemann–Roch via Chern character
nodes.description: The Chern character ch: K₀(X) → CH*(X)_ℚ becomes a ring isomorphism after tensoring with ℚ, with the Todd class correction giving Grothendieck–Riemann–Roch.

nodes.name: Rigid analytic space
nodes.description: A space obtained by gluing affinoid algebras over a non-archimedean field with a Grothendieck topology, providing p-adic analytic geometry.

nodes.name: Nakai–Moishezon criterion
nodes.description: A Cartier divisor D on a proper scheme is ample if and only if D^dim(V) · V > 0 for every positive-dimensional subvariety V.

nodes.name: Quantum group
nodes.description: A Hopf algebra deformation U_q(𝔤) of the universal enveloping algebra of a semisimple Lie algebra, introduced by Drinfeld and Jimbo.

nodes.name: Gorenstein ring
nodes.description: A commutative Noetherian local ring of finite injective dimension, equivalently a Cohen–Macaulay ring whose canonical module is free of rank one.

nodes.name: Local cohomology
nodes.description: The right derived functors H^i_I(M) of the I-torsion functor Γ_I on modules over a ring, measuring the failure of extending sections across the subscheme V(I).

nodes.name: Associated prime
nodes.description: A prime ideal p of a ring R is associated to an R-module M if p = Ann(m) for some m ∈ M; the set Ass(M) controls zero-divisors and supports primary decomposition.

nodes.name: Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity
nodes.description: The leading coefficient (times d!) of the Hilbert–Samuel polynomial measuring the asymptotic growth of lengths ℓ(M/I^n M), a fundamental multiplicity in local algebra.

nodes.name: Hilbert polynomial
nodes.description: The polynomial P(n) agreeing with the Hilbert function dim_k(M_n) for large n, encoding the degree and dimension of a projective variety or graded module.

nodes.name: Discrete valuation ring
nodes.description: A principal ideal domain with exactly one non-zero maximal ideal, equivalently a regular local ring of dimension one, fundamental in arithmetic geometry.

nodes.name: I-adic completion of a ring
nodes.description: The inverse limit R̂ = lim←(R/Iⁿ) completing a ring R with respect to an ideal I, producing a complete local ring when I is maximal.

nodes.name: Global class field theory
nodes.description: The Artin map induces an isomorphism between the idèle class group modulo norms and the Galois group of the maximal abelian extension of a number field.

nodes.name: B-spline
nodes.description: A piecewise polynomial basis function with minimal support defined by a recurrence on knot vectors, fundamental to computational approximation theory and CAGD.

nodes.name: Calderón–Zygmund singular integral operator
nodes.description: A principal-value convolution operator with kernel satisfying size and smoothness conditions away from the diagonal, bounded on Lᵖ by the Calderón–Zygmund theorem.

nodes.name: Wave front set
nodes.description: The subset WF(u) ⊂ T*X \ 0 of the cotangent bundle encoding both the singular support and the codirections of non-smoothness of a distribution u, central to microlocal analysis.

nodes.name: Killing form
nodes.description: The symmetric bilinear form B(X,Y) = tr(ad(X) ad(Y)) on a Lie algebra, whose nondegeneracy characterizes semisimplicity.

nodes.name: Abstract root system
nodes.description: A finite set of vectors in a Euclidean space satisfying axioms of spanning, integrality, and reflection closure, abstracting root structure from Lie algebras.

nodes.name: Classification of simple Lie algebras
nodes.description: Every simple complex Lie algebra is isomorphic to one of the classical series A_n, B_n, C_n, D_n or the exceptional algebras G_2, F_4, E_6, E_7, E_8.

nodes.name: Weyl dimension formula
nodes.description: Expresses the dimension of an irreducible highest-weight representation as a product over positive roots of inner-product ratios.

nodes.name: Cartan decomposition
nodes.description: Decomposes a semisimple Lie algebra g = k + p into eigenspaces of a Cartan involution, yielding the global decomposition G = K exp(p).

nodes.name: Symmetric space
nodes.description: A Riemannian manifold where every point is an isolated fixed point of an involutive isometry, equivalently a quotient G/K of a Lie group by the fixed-point set of an involution.

nodes.name: Cartan classification of symmetric spaces
nodes.description: Classifies irreducible Riemannian symmetric spaces into types I-IV corresponding to compact/non-compact forms and their duality.

nodes.name: Invariant theory (Hilbert finiteness)
nodes.description: Hilbert's theorem that the ring of polynomial invariants of a reductive group acting on a finite-dimensional vector space is finitely generated.

nodes.name: Lie group exponential map
nodes.description: The map exp: g -> G from a Lie algebra to its Lie group defined by the time-one flow of left-invariant vector fields, providing a local diffeomorphism near the identity.

nodes.name: Adjoint representation
nodes.description: The representation Ad: G -> GL(g) of a Lie group on its Lie algebra by conjugation, with differential ad: g -> End(g) given by the Lie bracket.

nodes.name: Harish-Chandra isomorphism
nodes.description: Identifies the center of the universal enveloping algebra Z(U(g)) with the Weyl-group invariants of the symmetric algebra S(h)^W via a shift by the half-sum of positive roots.

nodes.name: Bruhat decomposition
nodes.description: Decomposes a reductive group G into double cosets G = ∐_{w in W} BwB indexed by the Weyl group, stratifying the flag variety into Schubert cells.

nodes.name: R-matrix (Yang-Baxter)
nodes.description: A solution R of the Yang-Baxter equation R₁₂R₁₃R₂₃ = R₂₃R₁₃R₁₂ in End(V⊗V), governing integrability of quantum systems and providing structure for quantum groups.

nodes.name: Iwasawa decomposition
nodes.description: Decomposes a semisimple Lie group as G = KAN where K is maximal compact, A is abelian, and N is nilpotent, generalizing the QR decomposition.

nodes.name: Quantum group (Drinfeld-Jimbo)
nodes.description: A one-parameter deformation U_q(g) of the universal enveloping algebra of a semisimple Lie algebra, forming a quasitriangular Hopf algebra.

nodes.name: Demazure character formula
nodes.description: Expresses the character of a Demazure module (B-submodule of an irreducible G-module) via iterated applications of Demazure operators.

nodes.name: Duflo theorem
nodes.description: Establishes that the Duflo map, a symmetrization twisted by the square root of the Jacobian of the exponential, is an algebra isomorphism from S(g)^g to Z(U(g)).

nodes.name: Weyl integration formula
nodes.description: Reduces integration of class functions on a compact Lie group to integration over a maximal torus weighted by the square of the Weyl denominator.

nodes.name: Harish-Chandra character formula
nodes.description: Gives an explicit formula for the distribution character of an irreducible admissible representation of a real reductive group in terms of orbital integrals.

nodes.name: Plancherel theorem for semisimple groups
nodes.description: Decomposes L²(G) for a real semisimple Lie group into a direct integral of irreducible unitary representations with an explicit Plancherel measure.

nodes.name: Langlands classification
nodes.description: Parametrizes irreducible admissible representations of a real reductive group by triples (M,sigma,nu) consisting of Levi subgroup, tempered representation, and Langlands parameter.

nodes.name: Steinberg representation
nodes.description: The irreducible representation of a reductive group over a finite field whose dimension equals the largest power of p dividing |G(F_q)|, appearing in the cohomology of the Tits building.

nodes.name: Jackson's theorem
nodes.description: Gives upper bounds on the best polynomial approximation error E_n(f) in terms of the modulus of continuity, establishing direct theorems in approximation theory.

nodes.name: Bernstein inverse theorem
nodes.description: The converse of Jackson's theorem: if E_n(f) = O(n^{-r-alpha}) then f has r continuous derivatives with the r-th derivative in Lip(alpha).

nodes.name: Best approximation (Chebyshev)
nodes.description: The element of a finite-dimensional subspace minimizing the supremum-norm distance to a given continuous function, whose existence is guaranteed by compactness.

nodes.name: Chebyshev equioscillation theorem
nodes.description: A polynomial of degree n is the best uniform approximation to a continuous function if and only if the error equioscillates at least n+2 times.

nodes.name: Spline function
nodes.description: A piecewise polynomial of specified degree with prescribed smoothness conditions at the breakpoints (knots).

nodes.name: Schoenberg-Whitney theorem
nodes.description: B-spline interpolation at a set of data sites has a unique solution if and only if each B-spline is nonzero at at least one data site (the interlacing condition).

nodes.name: Scaling equation
nodes.description: The two-scale relation phi(x) = sum_k h_k phi(2x - k) satisfied by the scaling function in a multiresolution analysis, determining the associated wavelet.

nodes.name: Calderón-Zygmund singular integral operator
nodes.description: An L²-bounded operator whose distributional kernel satisfies standard size and regularity estimates away from the diagonal, generalizing the Hilbert transform.

nodes.name: Calderón-Zygmund decomposition (technique)
nodes.function_signature: (f in L^1, lambda > 0) -> (good part g in L^infty, bad part b supported on cubes)
nodes.description: Decomposes an integrable function at height lambda into a bounded good part and a bad part concentrated on cubes where the average exceeds lambda.

nodes.name: Parametrix
nodes.description: An approximate inverse of an elliptic (pseudo)differential operator, differing from the true inverse by a smoothing operator.

nodes.name: Fourier integral operator
nodes.description: A generalization of pseudodifferential operators defined by oscillatory integrals with a phase function parametrizing a Lagrangian submanifold, used to propagate singularities.

nodes.name: Hörmander propagation of singularities
nodes.description: For a principal-type operator P, the wave front set of a solution Pu = f propagates along the null bicharacteristic flow of the principal symbol.

nodes.name: Besov space
nodes.description: The function space B^s_{p,q} defined by Littlewood-Paley decomposition with l^q summability of frequency-localized pieces, interpolating between Sobolev and Hölder spaces.

nodes.name: Mikhlin multiplier theorem
nodes.description: A Fourier multiplier m(xi) defines an L^p-bounded operator for 1 < p < infty if m satisfies |xi^alpha D^alpha m| <= C for |alpha| <= [n/2] + 1.

nodes.name: Kolmogorov superposition theorem
nodes.description: Every continuous function of n variables can be represented as a finite superposition of continuous functions of one variable and addition.

nodes.name: Shannon sampling theorem
nodes.description: A bandlimited function with frequencies in [-W,W] is completely determined by and reconstructible from its samples taken at rate 2W.

nodes.name: Kotelnikov-Shannon-Whittaker interpolation
nodes.description: Reconstructs a bandlimited function from uniform samples using the sinc interpolation formula f(t) = sum_n f(n/2W) sinc(2Wt - n).

nodes.name: Symbol calculus
nodes.function_signature: (pseudodifferential operators P, Q) -> (composition symbol, parametrix symbol)
nodes.description: The algebraic framework for computing compositions, adjoints, and parametrices of pseudodifferential operators via asymptotic expansion of symbols.

nodes.name: Leray spectral sequence
nodes.description: A spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = H^p(B, R^q f_* F) converging to H^{p+q}(X, F) for a continuous map f: X -> B, relating sheaf cohomology of total and base spaces.

nodes.name: Grothendieck spectral sequence
nodes.description: For composable left-exact functors F, G with G sending injectives to F-acyclics, a spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = R^p F(R^q G(-)) converging to R^{p+q}(F ∘ G)(-).

nodes.name: Riemann-Hilbert correspondence
nodes.description: An equivalence between the category of regular holonomic D-modules and the category of perverse sheaves (constructible sheaves), generalizing the monodromy correspondence.

nodes.name: Wall groups L_n(π)
nodes.description: Algebraic L-groups of a group ring that classify surgery obstructions for manifolds with fundamental group π.

nodes.name: Surgery exact sequence
nodes.function_signature: (Poincaré complex X, normal data) → (structure set S(X), normal invariants, Wall groups)
nodes.description: Long exact sequence relating the structure set of a manifold to normal invariants and surgery obstruction groups.

nodes.name: Surgery obstruction
nodes.description: Element in a Wall L-group that vanishes if and only if a normal map is normally cobordant to a homotopy equivalence.

nodes.name: Normal invariant
nodes.description: Element of [X, G/O] classifying lifts of the Spivak normal fibration to a vector bundle, the first step in the surgery program.

nodes.name: Poincaré duality complex
nodes.description: Finite CW complex satisfying Poincaré duality with a fundamental class, serving as the homotopy-theoretic model of a closed manifold.

nodes.name: Spivak normal fibration
nodes.description: Stable spherical fibration over a Poincaré duality complex that plays the role of the stable normal bundle for manifolds.

nodes.name: Assembly map
nodes.description: Map from the homology of the classifying space with L-theory coefficients to the L-groups, whose injectivity is the Novikov conjecture.

nodes.name: Novikov conjecture
nodes.description: Conjecture that higher signatures of a closed oriented manifold are homotopy invariants, equivalent to rational injectivity of the assembly map.

nodes.name: Borel conjecture
nodes.description: Conjecture that every homotopy equivalence between closed aspherical manifolds is homotopic to a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Oriented cobordism ring Ω^SO_*
nodes.description: Graded ring of cobordism classes of oriented manifolds, computed by Thom, Wall, and others as a polynomial ring over ℤ tensored with 2-torsion.

nodes.name: Complex cobordism ring MU_*
nodes.description: Coefficient ring of complex cobordism, isomorphic to the Lazard ring ℤ[x_1, x_2, …] classifying formal group laws.

nodes.name: Thom's cobordism theorem
nodes.description: Identifies unoriented cobordism groups π_*(MO) with homology of BO, proving Ω^O_n ≅ H_n(BO; ℤ/2) and computing the unoriented cobordism ring.

nodes.name: Formal group law of MU
nodes.description: Universal formal group law arising from complex cobordism via the first Chern class of the tensor product of complex line bundles.

nodes.name: Quillen's theorem (MU_* ≅ Lazard ring)
nodes.description: The coefficient ring of complex cobordism MU is canonically isomorphic to the Lazard ring classifying one-dimensional commutative formal group laws.

nodes.name: Landweber exact functor theorem
nodes.function_signature: (MU_*-module M satisfying Landweber exactness) → (generalized cohomology theory)
nodes.description: Produces a cohomology theory from an MU_*-module by tensoring with MU_*(X), provided the sequence (p, v_1, v_2, …) acts regularly.

nodes.name: Adams e-invariant
nodes.description: Invariant e: π_{2k-1}(S^0) → ℚ/ℤ detecting the image of the J-homomorphism via Chern character calculations in K-theory.

nodes.name: Chromatic homotopy theory
nodes.description: Framework organizing stable homotopy theory by height of formal group laws, decomposing the stable category into chromatic layers via Morava K-theories.

nodes.name: Morava K-theory K(n)
nodes.description: Family of generalized cohomology theories K(n) at a prime p, with coefficient ring 𝔽_p[v_n, v_n⁻¹], detecting height-n periodic phenomena in stable homotopy.

nodes.name: Nilpotence theorem (Devinatz–Hopkins–Smith)
nodes.description: A self-map of a finite spectrum is nilpotent if and only if it induces zero on all Morava K-theories, establishing chromatic detection.

nodes.name: Periodicity theorem (Hopkins–Smith)
nodes.description: Every type-n finite p-local spectrum admits a v_n-self-map, producing periodic families in stable homotopy groups.

nodes.name: Thick subcategory theorem (Hopkins–Smith)
nodes.description: The thick subcategories of finite p-local spectra form a chain C_0 ⊃ C_1 ⊃ ⋯ indexed by chromatic height.

nodes.name: Smash product theorem (Hopkins–Ravenel)
nodes.description: The smash product of L_n-local spectra is L_n-local, establishing good monoidal properties for chromatic localization.

nodes.name: Segal conjecture (Carlsson's theorem)
nodes.description: The Burnside ring of a finite group G maps isomorphically (after completion) to the zeroth stable cohomotopy of BG.

nodes.name: Atiyah–Patodi–Singer eta invariant
nodes.description: Spectral invariant η(D) = Σ sign(λ)|λ|^{-s}|_{s=0} measuring spectral asymmetry of a self-adjoint elliptic operator on a closed manifold.

nodes.name: Atiyah–Patodi–Singer index theorem
nodes.description: Index formula for elliptic operators on manifolds with boundary, involving the eta invariant as a boundary correction to the Atiyah–Singer integrand.

nodes.name: Families index theorem
nodes.description: Atiyah–Singer index theorem for families of elliptic operators parametrized by a base space, giving an element in the K-theory of the parameter space.

nodes.name: Chern character
nodes.description: Ring homomorphism ch: K^0(X) → H^{even}(X; ℚ) that becomes an isomorphism after tensoring with ℚ, computed via Chern classes.

nodes.name: Hirzebruch L-class
nodes.description: Characteristic class L(p_1, p_2, …) of a real vector bundle appearing in the Hirzebruch signature theorem: σ(M) = ⟨L(M), [M]⟩.

nodes.name: Â-genus
nodes.description: Multiplicative genus associated to the power series x/2 / sinh(x/2), equal to the index of the Dirac operator on a spin manifold by Atiyah–Singer.

nodes.name: Associated bundle
nodes.description: Fiber bundle P ×_G F obtained from a principal G-bundle P by replacing the fiber with a G-space F via the diagonal action.

nodes.name: Milnor's construction of classifying spaces
nodes.function_signature: (Topological group G) → (Universal principal G-bundle EG → BG)
nodes.description: Constructs the classifying space BG as the infinite join G * G * ⋯ , providing a contractible free G-space.

nodes.name: Clutching construction
nodes.function_signature: (Map f: S^{n-1} → G) → (Principal G-bundle over S^n)
nodes.description: Builds a bundle over a sphere by gluing trivial bundles over hemispheres using a transition function on the equator.

nodes.name: HOMFLY-PT polynomial
nodes.description: Two-variable knot invariant P(l,m) generalizing both the Jones and Alexander polynomials, defined by a skein relation.

nodes.name: Vassiliev (finite-type) invariants
nodes.description: Knot invariants vanishing on singular knots with more than n double points, forming a filtered space whose graded quotients are chord diagram functionals.

nodes.name: Kontsevich integral
nodes.function_signature: (Knot K) → (Element in completed algebra of chord diagrams)
nodes.description: Universal Vassiliev invariant given by an iterated integral formula that dominates all finite-type knot invariants.

nodes.name: Kauffman bracket
nodes.description: State-sum polynomial ⟨D⟩ of unoriented link diagrams defined by local smoothing rules, related to the Jones polynomial by a writhe normalization.

nodes.name: Alexander polynomial
nodes.description: Classical knot invariant Δ_K(t) computed from the infinite cyclic cover of the knot complement, equal to the order of the Alexander module.

nodes.name: Seifert surface
nodes.description: Compact oriented surface embedded in S^3 whose boundary is a given knot or link, used to compute the Alexander polynomial via the Seifert matrix.

nodes.name: Khovanov homology
nodes.description: Bigraded homology theory categorifying the Jones polynomial, whose graded Euler characteristic recovers the Jones polynomial.

nodes.name: Eight Thurston geometries
nodes.description: The eight maximal homogeneous Riemannian 3-dimensional geometries (E^3, S^3, H^3, S^2×ℝ, H^2×ℝ, Nil, Sol, SL₂(ℝ)̃) underlying Thurston's geometrization.

nodes.name: Kneser–Milnor decomposition
nodes.description: Every closed oriented 3-manifold decomposes uniquely as a connected sum of prime 3-manifolds.

nodes.name: Mapping class group
nodes.description: Group Mod(Σ) = π_0(Diff^+(Σ)) of isotopy classes of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of a surface Σ.

nodes.name: Dehn twist
nodes.description: Diffeomorphism of a surface obtained by cutting along a simple closed curve, twisting one side by 2π, and regluing; generates the mapping class group.

nodes.name: Kirby calculus
nodes.function_signature: (Framed link diagram) → (3- or 4-manifold via handle moves)
nodes.description: Combinatorial method for studying 3- and 4-manifolds through handle decompositions, using Kirby moves on framed link diagrams.

nodes.name: Cuntz algebra O_n
nodes.description: Simple purely infinite C*-algebra generated by n isometries with orthogonal ranges summing to the identity, with K_0(O_n) ≅ ℤ/(n-1).

nodes.name: Toeplitz algebra
nodes.description: C*-algebra generated by the unilateral shift on ℓ^2(ℕ), fitting in a short exact sequence 0 → K → T → C(S^1) → 0.

nodes.name: Irrational rotation algebra A_θ
nodes.description: C*-algebra generated by two unitaries U, V with VU = e^{2πiθ}UV, the prototypical noncommutative torus with K_0 ≅ ℤ^2.

nodes.name: Modular automorphism group
nodes.description: One-parameter group σ^φ_t of *-automorphisms of a von Neumann algebra canonically associated to a faithful normal state φ by Tomita–Takesaki theory.

nodes.name: Kirchberg–Phillips theorem
nodes.description: Purely infinite simple separable nuclear C*-algebras satisfying the UCT are classified up to isomorphism by their K-theory.

nodes.name: Spectral triple (Connes)
nodes.description: Triple (A, H, D) of a *-algebra, Hilbert space, and self-adjoint operator with compact resolvent encoding noncommutative Riemannian geometry.

nodes.name: Cyclic cohomology
nodes.description: Cohomology theory HC^*(A) for associative algebras introduced by Connes, serving as the noncommutative analogue of de Rham cohomology.

nodes.name: Connes–Chern character
nodes.description: Map from K-theory to cyclic cohomology that extends the classical Chern character to the noncommutative setting.

nodes.name: Hochschild cohomology
nodes.description: Cohomology HH^*(A, M) of an associative algebra A with coefficients in a bimodule M, related to cyclic cohomology by the SBI exact sequence.

nodes.name: Noncommutative torus
nodes.description: Smooth noncommutative manifold (A_θ^∞, H, D) obtained by equipping the irrational rotation algebra with a canonical spectral triple.

nodes.name: Connes index theorem for foliations
nodes.description: Index theorem for longitudinal elliptic operators along the leaves of a foliation, taking values in the K-theory of the foliation C*-algebra.

nodes.name: Kasparov KK-theory
nodes.description: Bivariant K-theory KK(A, B) for C*-algebras unifying K-theory and K-homology, with a composition product generalizing index pairings.

nodes.name: Kasparov product
nodes.description: Associative composition product in KK-theory that encodes index pairings, boundary maps, and functorial operations on C*-algebras.

nodes.name: Universal coefficient theorem for KK-theory
nodes.description: Short exact sequence 0 → Ext(K_*(A), K_*(B)) → KK(A,B) → Hom(K_*(A), K_*(B)) → 0 for A in the UCT class.

nodes.name: Baum–Connes conjecture
nodes.description: Conjecture that the assembly map μ: K^G_*(EG) → K_*(C*_r(G)) from equivariant K-homology to C*-algebra K-theory is an isomorphism.

nodes.name: Planar algebra
nodes.description: Algebraic structure introduced by Jones axiomatizing the standard invariant of a subfactor via planar tangles and their composition.

nodes.name: Free independence
nodes.description: Noncommutative analogue of classical independence where alternating centered products vanish, the foundational axiom of free probability.

nodes.name: R-transform (Voiculescu)
nodes.description: Analytic transform linearizing free additive convolution: R_{a+b} = R_a + R_b for freely independent a, b in a noncommutative probability space.

nodes.name: Free entropy (Voiculescu)
nodes.description: Noncommutative analogue χ(X_1,…,X_n) of Shannon entropy for tuples of self-adjoint operators, defined via microstate approximation by random matrices.

nodes.name: S-transform (Voiculescu)
nodes.description: Analytic transform linearizing free multiplicative convolution: S_{ab} = S_a · S_b for freely independent positive a, b.

nodes.name: KPZ equation
nodes.description: Stochastic PDE ∂_t h = ν∂²_x h + λ(∂_x h)² + ξ for random interface growth, with characteristic 1:2:3 scaling exponents.

nodes.name: KPZ universality class
nodes.description: Universality class of random growth models in 1+1 dimensions sharing Tracy–Widom fluctuations and 1:2:3 scaling exponents.

nodes.name: Stochastic heat equation
nodes.description: Linear SPDE ∂_t u = Δu + σ(u)ξ driven by space-time white noise, whose solution via Itô integration is the Hopf–Cole transform of KPZ.

nodes.name: Hairer's regularity structures
nodes.description: Framework for giving meaning to singular stochastic PDEs by replacing Taylor polynomials with model-dependent local approximations and renormalization.

nodes.name: Paracontrolled distributions
nodes.description: Approach by Gubinelli–Imkeller–Perkowski to singular SPDEs using Bony paraproduct decomposition to define products of distributions.

nodes.name: Random matrix theory
nodes.description: Study of eigenvalue distributions of large random matrices, connecting probability, mathematical physics, and number theory via universality phenomena.

nodes.name: Sine kernel universality (bulk)
nodes.description: Universal local eigenvalue statistics in the bulk of the spectrum of Wigner matrices, with correlation kernel converging to sin(π(x-y))/(π(x-y)).

nodes.name: Dyson Brownian motion
nodes.description: Stochastic process of eigenvalues of a matrix-valued Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, with repulsive log-gas interaction between particles.

nodes.name: Russo–Seymour–Welsh estimates
nodes.description: Scale-invariant lower bounds on crossing probabilities for rectangles in critical percolation, key to proving conformal invariance.

nodes.name: Smirnov's theorem (critical site percolation)
nodes.description: Conformal invariance of crossing probabilities for critical site percolation on the triangular lattice, proved via discrete holomorphicity.

nodes.name: Contact process
nodes.description: Interacting particle system modeling infection spread where occupied sites infect neighbors at rate λ and recover at rate 1, exhibiting a phase transition.

nodes.name: Voter model
nodes.description: Interacting particle system where each site adopts the opinion of a random neighbor at rate 1, with clustering behavior depending on spatial dimension.

nodes.name: Exclusion process
nodes.description: Interacting particle system where particles perform random walks subject to the exclusion rule of at most one particle per site.

nodes.name: Hydrodynamic limit
nodes.description: Scaling limit of interacting particle systems where the empirical density profile converges to the solution of a macroscopic PDE.

nodes.name: Liggett ergodic theorem for IPS
nodes.description: Characterization of the ergodic behavior of attractive interacting particle systems via comparison with product measures.

nodes.name: Malliavin's probabilistic proof of Hörmander's theorem
nodes.description: Proof that hypoellipticity of Hörmander-type operators follows from the non-degeneracy of the Malliavin covariance matrix of the associated SDE.

nodes.name: Rough path theory (Lyons)
nodes.description: Extension of classical integration to paths of low regularity by enriching paths with iterated integral data (signature), enabling pathwise stochastic calculus.

nodes.name: Lyons universal limit theorem
nodes.description: Continuity of the Itô map from rough paths to solution paths in p-variation topology, providing pathwise stability for SDEs.

nodes.name: Lyons extension theorem
nodes.description: A rough path defined up to level ⌊p⌋ uniquely determines the full signature and hence all rough integrals against it.

nodes.name: Gubinelli controlled rough paths
nodes.function_signature: (Rough path X, controlled integrand Y) → (Rough integral ∫Y dX)
nodes.description: Simplified approach to rough integration where integrands controlled by a reference rough path can be integrated via a sewing-type argument.

nodes.name: Sewing lemma
nodes.description: Key technical lemma in rough path theory providing existence and uniqueness of a limit for approximately additive functionals on partitions.

nodes.name: SLE phases (κ ≤ 4, 4 < κ < 8, κ ≥ 8)
nodes.description: Phase diagram of SLE_κ: simple curves for κ ≤ 4, self-touching curves for 4 < κ < 8, and space-filling curves for κ ≥ 8.

nodes.name: SLE/CFT correspondence
nodes.description: Identification of SLE_κ partition functions with conformal field theory correlators at central charge c = (6-κ)(3κ-8)/(2κ).

nodes.name: Yang–Mills connection
nodes.description: Connection on a principal G-bundle that is a critical point of the Yang–Mills functional ∫|F_A|^2, generalizing Maxwell's equations to nonabelian gauge groups.

nodes.name: BPST instanton
nodes.description: Explicit self-dual SU(2) connection on S^4 with instanton number 1, discovered by Belavin–Polyakov–Schwarz–Tyupkin, minimizing Yang–Mills energy in its topological class.

nodes.name: Uhlenbeck removable singularity theorem
nodes.description: A Yang–Mills connection on a punctured 4-ball with finite energy extends smoothly across the puncture after a gauge transformation.

nodes.name: Chern–Simons functional
nodes.description: Secondary characteristic class functional CS(A) = ∫ tr(A∧dA + ⅔A∧A∧A) on connections over a 3-manifold, whose critical points are flat connections.

nodes.name: Sugawara construction
nodes.description: Realization of the Virasoro algebra as quadratic expressions in affine Lie algebra currents, yielding the energy-momentum tensor for WZW models.

nodes.name: Modular functor
nodes.description: Functor from the category of surfaces with boundary to vector spaces, satisfying gluing axioms, encoding the algebraic structure of a 2D conformal field theory.

nodes.name: KdV soliton
nodes.description: Solitary wave solution u(x,t) = -c/2 · sech²(√c/2 · (x - ct)) of the KdV equation, preserving shape after interaction with other solitons.

nodes.name: Zakharov–Shabat system
nodes.description: Generalized eigenvalue problem (Lax pair) for the AKNS hierarchy, extending inverse scattering to the nonlinear Schrödinger and sine-Gordon equations.

nodes.name: Hitchin system
nodes.description: Algebraically completely integrable Hamiltonian system on the moduli space of Higgs bundles over a Riemann surface, with spectral curve fibration.

nodes.name: KP hierarchy
nodes.description: Infinite system of integrable PDEs in 2+1 dimensions generalizing KdV, with solutions parametrized by points of the Sato Grassmannian.

nodes.name: Drinfeld–Jimbo quantum group U_q(𝔤)
nodes.description: Hopf algebra deformation of the universal enveloping algebra of a semisimple Lie algebra, with generators and q-deformed Serre relations.

nodes.name: Quantum R-matrix
nodes.description: Solution R ∈ End(V⊗V) of the quantum Yang–Baxter equation providing braiding in the category of quantum group representations.

nodes.name: Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants
nodes.function_signature: (3-manifold M, modular tensor category C) → (Complex number RT_C(M))
nodes.description: Topological invariants of 3-manifolds constructed from surgery presentations using the representation theory of quantum groups.

nodes.name: Atiyah's TQFT axioms
nodes.description: Axioms defining a topological quantum field theory as a symmetric monoidal functor from the cobordism category to the category of vector spaces.

nodes.name: Witten–Chern–Simons TQFT
nodes.description: Three-dimensional TQFT arising from Chern–Simons gauge theory with compact gauge group, producing the Jones polynomial and its generalizations.

nodes.name: Turaev–Viro invariant
nodes.description: State-sum invariant of 3-manifolds defined from a triangulation using quantum 6j-symbols, equivalent to the square modulus of the Reshetikhin–Turaev invariant.

nodes.name: Dijkgraaf–Witten invariant
nodes.description: Finite-group TQFT invariant of 3-manifolds obtained by summing a cocycle weight over gauge equivalence classes of principal G-bundles.

nodes.name: Ising model
nodes.description: Statistical mechanics lattice model with spins σ_i = ±1 interacting via nearest-neighbor coupling H = -J Σ σ_iσ_j, exhibiting a ferromagnetic phase transition.

nodes.name: Gopakumar–Vafa invariants
nodes.description: Integer-valued curve-counting invariants of a Calabi–Yau threefold, conjecturally equivalent to Gromov–Witten invariants via a BPS state reorganization.

nodes.name: Donaldson–Thomas invariants
nodes.description: Virtual counts of ideal sheaves on a Calabi–Yau threefold, related to Gromov–Witten invariants by the MNOP conjecture.

nodes.name: Supermanifold
nodes.description: Ringed space locally modeled on (ℝ^m|n, C^∞ ⊗ ∧ℝ^n) with commuting and anticommuting coordinates, the geometric setting of supersymmetry.

nodes.name: Super Lie algebra
nodes.description: ℤ/2-graded algebra with a bracket satisfying graded antisymmetry and the graded Jacobi identity, generalizing Lie algebras to include fermionic generators.

nodes.name: Spectral zeta function
nodes.description: Zeta function ζ_D(s) = Σ λ_n^{-s} formed from eigenvalues of an elliptic operator, whose special values encode spectral invariants via zeta regularization.

nodes.name: Heat kernel asymptotic expansion
nodes.description: Small-time expansion tr(e^{-tΔ}) ~ (4πt)^{-d/2} Σ a_k t^k as t→0, with coefficients a_k encoding local geometric invariants of the manifold.

nodes.name: Spectral invariants
nodes.description: Geometric quantities determined by the spectrum of the Laplacian, including dimension, volume, and total scalar curvature, via the heat kernel expansion.

nodes.name: Scattering matrix (PDE)
nodes.description: Unitary operator S = W_+^* W_- relating incoming and outgoing asymptotic states in quantum scattering theory via the Møller wave operators.

nodes.name: Møller wave operators
nodes.description: Strong limits W_± = s-lim_{t→±∞} e^{iHt} e^{-iH_0t} intertwining the free and full Hamiltonians in scattering theory.

nodes.name: Asymptotic completeness
nodes.description: Statement that the ranges of the Møller wave operators span the absolutely continuous subspace of the full Hamiltonian, so all scattering states scatter.

nodes.name: Limiting absorption principle
nodes.description: Boundary values of the resolvent (H - λ ± iε)^{-1} exist as bounded operators between weighted spaces as ε → 0, yielding unique outgoing solutions.

nodes.name: Mourre estimate
nodes.description: Positive commutator estimate E_Δ i[H,A] E_Δ ≥ θ E_Δ implying the limiting absorption principle and absence of singular continuous spectrum on Δ.

nodes.name: Compensated compactness
nodes.function_signature: (Sequences with PDE constraints) → (Weak continuity of nonlinear quantities)
nodes.description: Method of Murat–Tartar showing that certain nonlinear expressions pass to the weak limit when the sequences satisfy differential constraints.

nodes.name: Div-curl lemma
nodes.description: If E_n ⇀ E with curl E_n bounded and B_n ⇀ B with div B_n bounded, then E_n · B_n ⇀ E · B in the sense of distributions.

nodes.name: Crandall–Ishii lemma
nodes.description: Maximum principle for semicontinuous functions providing second-order jet estimates at points where a difference touches its maximum, fundamental for viscosity solution theory.

nodes.name: Stefan problem
nodes.description: Free boundary problem modeling phase transitions (melting/solidification) where the interface velocity equals the jump in heat flux across the phase boundary.

nodes.name: Caffarelli free boundary regularity
nodes.description: Regularity theory for the free boundary in the obstacle problem: the free boundary is C^{1,α} near regular points where the contact set has positive density.

nodes.name: Alt–Caffarelli–Friedman monotonicity formula
nodes.description: Monotonicity formula for pairs of nonnegative subharmonic functions with disjoint supports, a key tool for free boundary regularity in two-phase problems.

nodes.name: Homogenization theorem (elliptic)
nodes.description: Solutions u^ε of -div(A(x/ε)∇u^ε) = f converge as ε → 0 to the solution of -div(A^{hom}∇u) = f with constant effective coefficients A^{hom}.

nodes.name: Cell problem (homogenization)
nodes.description: Periodic boundary value problem on the unit cell whose solution determines the effective homogenized coefficients A^{hom} via averaging.

nodes.name: Two-scale convergence
nodes.description: Convergence notion where u^ε(x) ⇀ u_0(x,y) in the sense of testing against oscillatory functions φ(x, x/ε), capturing both macroscopic and microscopic behavior.

nodes.name: Γ-convergence
nodes.description: Variational convergence of functionals ensuring that minimizers converge to minimizers of the limit functional, fundamental in homogenization and phase field models.

nodes.name: Matroid rank function
nodes.description: Function r: 2^E → ℤ satisfying r(∅) = 0, monotonicity, and submodularity, providing a cryptomorphic axiomatization of matroids.

nodes.name: Tutte polynomial
nodes.description: Two-variable polynomial T_M(x,y) of a matroid M encoding deletion-contraction invariants, specializing to chromatic, flow, and reliability polynomials.

nodes.name: Matroid union theorem
nodes.description: The union of k matroids on E is again a matroid, with rank function r(A) = min_{A₁∪⋯∪A_k=A} Σ r_i(A_i).

nodes.name: Rado's theorem (matroid transversals)
nodes.description: A family of sets (A_i) admits a system of distinct representatives belonging to an independent set of a matroid if and only if the rank condition r(∪_{i∈J} A_i) ≥ |J| holds for all J.

nodes.name: Matroid duality
nodes.description: Every matroid M on ground set E has a dual matroid M* whose bases are complements of bases of M, satisfying (M*)* = M.

nodes.name: Maximum distance separable (MDS) codes
nodes.description: Linear codes meeting the Singleton bound d = n - k + 1 with equality, including Reed–Solomon codes as the primary example.

nodes.name: BCH code
nodes.description: Cyclic error-correcting code defined by roots that are consecutive powers of a primitive element, with designed distance guaranteeing error-correction capability.

nodes.name: Turbo and LDPC codes
nodes.description: Capacity-approaching codes using iterative decoding: turbo codes via parallel concatenation with interleaving, LDPC codes via sparse parity-check matrices.

nodes.name: Elliptic curve cryptography
nodes.description: Public-key cryptography based on the discrete logarithm problem in the group of rational points on an elliptic curve over a finite field.

nodes.name: Lattice-based cryptography
nodes.description: Cryptographic constructions whose security relies on the hardness of lattice problems such as LWE and SVP, conjectured to be post-quantum secure.

nodes.name: Learning with errors (LWE)
nodes.description: Computational problem of distinguishing noisy linear equations mod q from uniform, forming the basis of lattice-based cryptographic schemes.

nodes.name: Balanced incomplete block design (BIBD)
nodes.description: Collection of b blocks of size k from v points such that every pair of points appears in exactly λ blocks, satisfying bk = vr and r(k-1) = λ(v-1).

nodes.name: Fisher's inequality
nodes.description: In a non-trivial BIBD, the number of blocks b is at least the number of points v, proved using the rank of the incidence matrix.

nodes.name: Latin square
nodes.description: An n × n array filled with n different symbols, each occurring exactly once in each row and column, equivalent to the Cayley table of a quasigroup.

nodes.name: Witt design
nodes.description: The unique 5-(24,8,1) Steiner system S(5,8,24) associated to the Mathieu group M₂₄, with remarkable combinatorial and group-theoretic properties.

nodes.name: Graphon
nodes.description: Measurable symmetric function W: [0,1]² → [0,1] arising as the limit of dense graph sequences in the cut metric, the basic object of graph limit theory.

nodes.name: Lovász–Szegedy theorem
nodes.description: A sequence of dense graphs converges in the cut metric if and only if all subgraph densities converge, and the limit is a graphon.

nodes.name: Density Hales–Jewett theorem
nodes.description: For any δ > 0 and alphabet size k, sufficiently high-dimensional combinatorial subspaces of [k]^n must contain a combinatorial line in any set of density δ.

nodes.name: Intersection cohomology
nodes.description: Cohomology theory IH^*(X) for singular spaces introduced by Goresky–MacPherson, restoring Poincaré duality by imposing allowability conditions on chains.

nodes.name: BBD decomposition theorem
nodes.description: For a proper morphism f: X → Y of varieties, the direct image Rf_*IC_X decomposes as a direct sum of shifted simple perverse sheaves on Y.

nodes.name: D-module
nodes.description: Module over the sheaf of algebraic differential operators on a variety, providing an algebraic framework for systems of linear PDEs and the Riemann–Hilbert correspondence.

nodes.name: Beilinson–Bernstein localization
nodes.description: Equivalence between the category of D-modules on the flag variety G/B and modules over U(𝔤) with a fixed central character, algebraizing representation theory.

nodes.name: Springer correspondence
nodes.description: Bijection between irreducible representations of the Weyl group and pairs (nilpotent orbit, local system) via the cohomology of Springer fibers.

nodes.name: Geometric Satake equivalence
nodes.description: Equivalence between the category of perverse sheaves on the affine Grassmannian of G and the representation category of the Langlands dual group G^∨.

nodes.name: Weyl module
nodes.description: Universal highest weight module V(λ) for a reductive algebraic group in positive characteristic, the characteristic-p analogue of a finite-dimensional simple module.

nodes.name: Lusztig conjecture
nodes.description: Conjecture expressing characters of simple modules for reductive groups in characteristic p in terms of Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials, proved for large p.

nodes.name: Steinberg tensor product theorem
nodes.description: Decomposes simple modules for reductive groups in characteristic p as tensor products of Frobenius twists of restricted simple modules.

nodes.name: Jantzen filtration
nodes.description: Canonical filtration of a Weyl module by submodules with character sum given by an alternating sum formula involving Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials.

nodes.name: Langlands dual group G^∨
nodes.description: Reductive group whose root datum is dual to that of G (interchanging roots and coroots), fundamental to the Langlands correspondence.

nodes.name: Langlands L-function
nodes.description: L-function L(s, π, r) attached to an automorphic representation π and a representation r of the L-group, generalizing Hecke and Artin L-functions.

nodes.name: Arthur's endoscopic classification
nodes.description: Classification of automorphic representations of classical groups via Arthur parameters and endoscopic transfer from GL(N).

nodes.name: Fundamental lemma (Ngô)
nodes.description: Identity of orbital integrals for a reductive group and its endoscopic groups, proved by Ngô using the geometry of the Hitchin fibration.

nodes.name: Geometric Langlands conjecture
nodes.description: Conjectural equivalence between D-modules on Bun_G and quasi-coherent sheaves on Loc_{G^∨} for a smooth projective curve, geometrizing the Langlands program.

nodes.name: Hecke eigensheaf
nodes.description: D-module on Bun_G that is an eigenvector for all Hecke operators, the geometric analogue of a Hecke eigenform in the geometric Langlands program.

nodes.name: Reynolds operator
nodes.description: Projection R: k[V] → k[V]^G onto the ring of invariants by averaging over the group action, existing when the group is linearly reductive.

nodes.name: Molien's formula
nodes.description: Hilbert series of the ring of invariants k[V]^G equals 1/|G| Σ_{g∈G} 1/det(I - tg), computing the dimensions of graded components.

nodes.name: Chevalley–Shephard–Todd theorem
nodes.description: The ring of invariants k[V]^G is a polynomial ring if and only if G is generated by pseudo-reflections.

nodes.name: Hilbert–Mumford criterion
nodes.description: A point is GIT-(semi)stable if and only if it is (semi)stable for all one-parameter subgroups, reducing stability to a numerical check on weights.

nodes.name: First fundamental theorem of invariant theory
nodes.description: For the classical groups (GL, O, Sp), the ring of polynomial invariants on V^⊕n is generated by specific contractions (inner products, determinants).

nodes.name: Second fundamental theorem of invariant theory
nodes.description: Describes the ideal of relations among the generators given by the first fundamental theorem for the classical groups.

nodes.name: Pontryagin–Thom (framed cobordism)
nodes.description: Bijection between framed cobordism classes of framed submanifolds in S^{n+k} and π_{n+k}(S^n), the original formulation of the Pontryagin–Thom construction.

nodes.name: Cobordism hypothesis (Baez–Dolan)
nodes.description: A fully extended n-dimensional TQFT is determined by its value on a point, which must be a fully dualizable object in the target (∞,n)-category.

nodes.name: Nuclear C*-algebra
nodes.description: C*-algebra A for which every C*-tensor product with another C*-algebra is unique, equivalently admitting a completely positive approximation by finite-rank maps.

nodes.name: Exact C*-algebra
nodes.description: C*-algebra A such that the reduced cross product by A preserves short exact sequences of C*-algebras, equivalently embeddable in a nuclear C*-algebra.

nodes.name: Formal language
nodes.description: A precisely specified system of signs, assemblies (terms and relations), and syntactic rules for constructing well-formed expressions.

nodes.name: Quantifier (universal, existential)
nodes.description: The operators for-all and exists that bind a variable in a relation to express universal or existential properties.

nodes.name: Axiom scheme of substitution (logic)
nodes.description: The logical scheme permitting replacement of a free variable by a term in any well-formed relation, subject to no variable capture.

nodes.name: Modus ponens
nodes.description: The fundamental rule of inference: from A and A => B, deduce B.

nodes.name: Deductive system
nodes.description: The formal framework of proofs as finite sequences of relations, each an axiom or derived by rules of inference; a theorem is the final relation.

nodes.name: Hilbert epsilon operator (tau-operator)
nodes.description: A term-forming operator tau_x(R) selecting an object satisfying relation R if one exists, used to eliminate quantifiers and formalize choice at the logical level.

nodes.name: Axiom of the empty set
nodes.description: There exists a set having no elements, denoted empty-set.

nodes.name: Axiom of pairing
nodes.description: For any two objects a, b, there exists a set {a, b} whose only elements are a and b.

nodes.name: Axiom scheme of separation (comprehension)
nodes.description: For any set A and property P(x), there exists the set {x in A : P(x)} of exactly those elements of A satisfying P.

nodes.name: Axiom of union
nodes.description: For any set of sets F, there exists a set whose elements are exactly those belonging to at least one member of F.

nodes.name: Set membership (element-of relation)
nodes.description: The primitive binary relation x in A asserting that x is an element of the set A.

nodes.name: Subset (inclusion)
nodes.description: A subset-of B means every element of A is an element of B, defining the inclusion partial order on sets.

nodes.name: Set intersection
nodes.description: A cap B = {x : x in A and x in B}, the set of elements common to both A and B.

nodes.name: Set union (binary)
nodes.description: A cup B = {x : x in A or x in B}, the set of elements belonging to at least one of A, B.

nodes.name: Set complement (difference)
nodes.description: A \ B = {x in A : x not in B}, the set of elements in A but not in B.

nodes.name: Symmetric difference
nodes.description: A triangle B = (A \ B) u (B \ A), the set of elements belonging to exactly one of A, B.

nodes.name: Ordered pair
nodes.description: The object (a, b) defined via Kuratowski encoding such that (a,b) = (c,d) iff a = c and b = d.

nodes.name: Cartesian product
nodes.description: A x B = {(a, b) : a in A, b in B}, the set of all ordered pairs with first component in A and second in B.

nodes.name: Relation (graph of a relation)
nodes.description: A subset R of A x B; one writes xRy to mean (x, y) in R.

nodes.name: Function (map, mapping)
nodes.description: A relation f subset A x B such that for every a in A there exists exactly one b in B with (a, b) in f, written f : A -> B.

nodes.name: Injection (one-to-one map)
nodes.description: A function f : A -> B such that f(a1) = f(a2) implies a1 = a2.

nodes.name: Surjection (onto map)
nodes.description: A function f : A -> B such that for every b in B there exists a in A with f(a) = b.

nodes.name: Bijection
nodes.description: A function that is both injective and surjective, establishing a one-to-one correspondence.

nodes.name: Composition of functions
nodes.description: Given f : A -> B and g : B -> C, the composite g o f : A -> C defined by (g o f)(a) = g(f(a)).

nodes.name: Inverse function
nodes.description: For a bijection f : A -> B, the unique function f^{-1} : B -> A satisfying f^{-1} o f = id_A and f o f^{-1} = id_B.

nodes.name: Image and preimage
nodes.description: For f : A -> B, the direct image f(S) = {f(x) : x in S} and the inverse image f^{-1}(T) = {x in A : f(x) in T}.

nodes.name: Restriction and extension of a function
nodes.description: The restriction f|_S of f : A -> B to S subset A; an extension of g : S -> B is any f : A -> B with f|_S = g.

nodes.name: Family of sets (indexed family)
nodes.description: A function i -> A_i from an index set I to a collection of sets, written (A_i)_{i in I}.

nodes.name: Generalized union and intersection
nodes.description: For a family (A_i)_{i in I}, the union U_{i in I} A_i and intersection cap_{i in I} A_i, generalizing binary operations to arbitrary index sets.

nodes.name: Generalized Cartesian product (product of a family)
nodes.description: Product_{i in I} A_i, the set of all choice functions on the family, each selecting an element from A_i for every i.

nodes.name: Equivalence relation
nodes.description: A relation R on a set A that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive.

nodes.name: Equivalence class
nodes.description: For an equivalence relation R on A, the class [a] = {x in A : xRa}.

nodes.name: Quotient set
nodes.description: A/R = {[a] : a in A}, the set of all equivalence classes, with canonical surjection pi : A -> A/R.

nodes.name: Canonical decomposition of a map
nodes.description: Every function f : A -> B factors uniquely as A -> A/~ -> f(A) -> B (surjection, bijection, inclusion).

nodes.name: Partition of a set
nodes.description: A family of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets whose union is A, in canonical bijection with equivalence relations on A.

nodes.name: Diagonal of a product
nodes.description: Delta_A = {(a, a) : a in A} subset A x A, the graph of the identity function.

nodes.name: Projection map
nodes.description: The canonical surjections pr_1 : A x B -> A and pr_2 : A x B -> B extracting components of an ordered pair.

nodes.name: Preorder (quasi-order)
nodes.description: A reflexive and transitive relation, not necessarily antisymmetric; the quotient by the associated equivalence is a partial order.

nodes.name: Strict partial order
nodes.description: The irreflexive and transitive relation < derived from <= by x < y iff x <= y and x != y.

nodes.name: Greatest element and least element
nodes.description: In a poset, a greatest (resp. least) element a satisfies x <= a (resp. a <= x) for all x.

nodes.name: Supremum and infimum
nodes.description: sup S is the least upper bound of S; inf S is the greatest lower bound of S, when they exist.

nodes.name: Lattice
nodes.description: A poset in which every pair of elements has both a supremum (join) and an infimum (meet).

nodes.name: Complete lattice
nodes.description: A poset in which every subset has a supremum and an infimum.

nodes.name: Directed set
nodes.description: A nonempty preordered set in which every finite subset has an upper bound.

nodes.name: Increasing (order-preserving) map
nodes.description: A function f between posets such that x <= y implies f(x) <= f(y).

nodes.name: Order isomorphism
nodes.description: A bijection f between posets such that both f and f^{-1} are order-preserving.

nodes.name: Chain (totally ordered subset)
nodes.description: A subset of a poset that is totally ordered under the induced order.

nodes.name: Well-ordered set
nodes.description: A totally ordered set in which every nonempty subset has a least element.

nodes.name: Hausdorff maximality principle
nodes.description: Every partially ordered set contains a maximal chain; equivalent to axiom of choice.

nodes.name: Initial segment (section)
nodes.description: In a well-ordered set W, the set S_a = {x in W : x < a} of all elements strictly preceding a.

nodes.name: Comparability of well-ordered sets
nodes.description: Any two well-ordered sets are comparable: one is order-isomorphic to an initial segment of the other.

nodes.name: Cantor's theorem
nodes.description: For any set A, there is no surjection from A onto P(A); equivalently |A| < |P(A)|.

nodes.name: Equipotence (equinumerosity)
nodes.description: Two sets are equipotent if there exists a bijection between them.

nodes.name: Finite set
nodes.description: A set equipotent to some natural number {0, 1, ..., n-1}.

nodes.name: Countable set (denumerable)
nodes.description: A set equipotent to a subset of the natural numbers; countably infinite if equipotent to N.

nodes.name: Disjoint union (coproduct of sets)
nodes.description: A disjoint-union B = (A x {0}) u (B x {1}), a union keeping copies distinct even when they overlap.

nodes.name: Absorption law for infinite cardinals
nodes.description: For an infinite cardinal kappa, kappa + kappa = kappa * kappa = kappa.

nodes.name: Mathematical induction
nodes.description: If P(0) holds and P(n) => P(n+1), then P(n) holds for all natural numbers n.

nodes.name: Arithmetic of natural numbers
nodes.description: Addition and multiplication on N defined by recursion, satisfying commutativity, associativity, distributivity.

nodes.name: Order on natural numbers
nodes.description: The total order on N where m <= n iff m subset n (as sets), making (N, <=) a well-ordered set.

nodes.name: Species of structures
nodes.description: Bourbaki's formal specification: base sets, auxiliary sets, typification via echelon construction, and an axiom invariant under transport.

nodes.name: Echelon construction type
nodes.description: A set obtained from base sets by iterated application of power set and Cartesian product, providing the type of a structure.

nodes.name: Isomorphism of structures
nodes.description: A bijection between base sets of two structures of the same species that transports one structure to the other.

nodes.name: Transport of structures
nodes.description: Transferring a structure from one set to another via a bijection, preserving all structural axioms.
nodes.function_signature: (Structure on A, Bijection A -> B) -> Structure on B

nodes.name: Induced structure (substructure)
nodes.description: The structure inherited by a subset of the base set, obtained by restricting the structural data.

nodes.name: Product structure
nodes.description: The structure on a Cartesian product obtained by combining the structures on each factor componentwise.

nodes.name: Quotient structure
nodes.description: The structure induced on a quotient set A/R when the equivalence relation R is compatible with the given structure.

nodes.name: Initial structure
nodes.description: The coarsest structure on a set making a given family of maps into structured sets into morphisms.

nodes.name: Final structure
nodes.description: The finest structure on a set making a given family of maps from structured sets into morphisms.

nodes.name: Morphism (of a species of structures)
nodes.description: A map between base sets that respects the structural data; the precise definition depends on the species.

nodes.name: Neighborhood filter
nodes.description: The filter V(x) of all neighborhoods of a point x in a topological space, whose properties characterize the topology.

nodes.name: Filter
nodes.description: A nonempty collection of subsets of a set X, closed under finite intersection and supersets, and not containing the empty set.

nodes.name: Filter base (basis of a filter)
nodes.description: A nonempty collection of nonempty subsets such that any two members contain a common refinement; it generates a filter.

nodes.name: Convergence of a filter
nodes.description: A filter F on a topological space converges to x if F is finer than the neighborhood filter of x, i.e., V(x) subset F.

nodes.name: Cluster point of a filter
nodes.description: A point x such that every neighborhood of x meets every set in the filter.

nodes.name: Continuous map
nodes.description: A function f : X -> Y between topological spaces such that the preimage of every open set in Y is open in X.

nodes.name: Open map and closed map
nodes.description: A map sending open (resp. closed) sets to open (resp. closed) sets.

nodes.name: Subspace topology (induced topology)
nodes.description: The topology on a subset A of X whose open sets are intersections of open sets of X with A.

nodes.name: Initial topology
nodes.description: The coarsest topology on X making a given family of maps f_i : X -> Y_i continuous, with subbase {f_i^{-1}(U_i)}.

nodes.name: Final topology
nodes.description: The finest topology on Y making a given family of maps g_i : X_i -> Y continuous.

nodes.name: Hausdorff space (T2)
nodes.description: A topological space in which any two distinct points have disjoint neighborhoods.

nodes.name: T1 space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every singleton {x} is closed.

nodes.name: Regular space (T3)
nodes.description: A T1 space in which each point and disjoint closed set can be separated by disjoint open sets.

nodes.name: Completely regular space (Tychonoff, T3.5)
nodes.description: A T1 space in which points and disjoint closed sets can be separated by continuous real-valued functions.

nodes.name: Limit of a function
nodes.description: f(x) -> l as x -> a along a filter means the image filter converges to l, unifying all notions of limit.

nodes.name: Net (Moore-Smith sequence)
nodes.description: A function from a directed set into a topological space, generalizing sequences.

nodes.name: Connected space
nodes.description: A topological space that cannot be expressed as the union of two disjoint nonempty open sets.

nodes.name: Connected component
nodes.description: The maximal connected subset containing a given point; connected components partition the space into closed sets.

nodes.name: Locally connected space
nodes.description: A space in which every point has a neighborhood base consisting of connected open sets.

nodes.name: Second-countable space
nodes.description: A topological space possessing a countable base for its topology.

nodes.name: First-countable space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every point has a countable neighborhood base.

nodes.name: Separable space
nodes.description: A topological space containing a countable dense subset.

nodes.name: Uniform space (uniformity)
nodes.description: A set X equipped with a filter on X x X (entourages) containing the diagonal, symmetric, and satisfying the triangle condition.

nodes.name: Entourage (surrounding)
nodes.description: A member V of the uniformity; V[x] = {y : (x,y) in V} is the V-neighborhood of x.

nodes.name: Uniform topology
nodes.description: The topology on a uniform space where U is open iff for each x in U there exists entourage V with V[x] subset U.

nodes.name: Uniformly continuous map
nodes.description: A function f between uniform spaces such that for every entourage W of Y, (f x f)^{-1}(W) is an entourage of X.

nodes.name: Cauchy filter
nodes.description: A filter on a uniform space such that for every entourage V, there exists F in the filter with F x F subset V.

nodes.name: Complete uniform space
nodes.description: A uniform space in which every Cauchy filter converges.

nodes.name: Completion of a uniform space
nodes.description: A complete Hausdorff uniform space X-hat with uniformly continuous dense embedding X -> X-hat, unique up to uniform isomorphism.

nodes.name: Uniform isomorphism
nodes.description: A bijection f between uniform spaces such that both f and f^{-1} are uniformly continuous.

nodes.name: Product uniformity
nodes.description: The coarsest uniformity on the product making all projections uniformly continuous.

nodes.name: Induced uniformity (subspace uniformity)
nodes.description: The uniformity on a subset A induced by restricting entourages to A x A.

nodes.name: Minimal Cauchy filter
nodes.description: A Cauchy filter minimal among all Cauchy filters, used in the construction of completions.

nodes.name: Left uniform structure on a topological group
nodes.description: The uniformity on G with entourage base {(x,y) : x^{-1}y in V} where V ranges over identity neighborhoods.

nodes.name: Subgroup topology
nodes.description: The subspace topology on a subgroup H of a topological group G, making H a topological group.

nodes.name: Quotient group topology
nodes.description: The quotient topology on G/H for a normal subgroup H, making G/H a topological group and projection open.

nodes.name: Closure of a subgroup
nodes.description: The closure of a subgroup in a topological group is again a subgroup; the closure of a normal subgroup is normal.

nodes.name: Neighborhood base at the identity
nodes.description: A topological group's topology is completely determined by a neighborhood base at identity e, since translation is a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Open subgroup theorem
nodes.description: Every open subgroup of a topological group is also closed; every subgroup containing an open subgroup is open.

nodes.name: Completion of a topological group
nodes.description: The Hausdorff completion of a topological group carries a canonical topological group structure.

nodes.name: Completeness of R (least upper bound property)
nodes.description: Every nonempty subset of R bounded above has a least upper bound (supremum) in R.

nodes.name: Archimedean property
nodes.description: For any real x > 0 and y, there exists natural n with nx > y; equivalently, Z is unbounded in R.

nodes.name: Density of Q in R
nodes.description: Between any two distinct real numbers there exists a rational number; Q is dense in R.

nodes.name: Order topology on R
nodes.description: The topology on R generated by open intervals (a, b), coinciding with the metric topology from |x - y|.

nodes.name: Extended real line
nodes.description: R-bar = R u {-inf, +inf}, a compact totally ordered space extending R with two points at infinity.

nodes.name: Absolute value (on R)
nodes.description: The function |x| = max(x, -x) on R, defining the standard metric d(x,y) = |x - y|.

nodes.name: Monotone convergence for sequences in R
nodes.description: Every bounded monotone sequence in R converges to its supremum (if increasing) or infimum (if decreasing).

nodes.name: Right and left limits
nodes.description: For a real function, f(a+) = lim_{x->a, x>a} f(x) and f(a-) = lim_{x->a, x<a} f(x).

nodes.name: Power function
nodes.description: x^alpha = exp(alpha ln x) for x > 0, extending integer powers to arbitrary real exponents.

nodes.name: Euclidean topology on R^n
nodes.description: The product topology on R^n, equivalently the metric topology from the Euclidean norm.

nodes.name: Normed vector space (over R)
nodes.description: A real vector space equipped with a norm satisfying positive definiteness, homogeneity, and the triangle inequality.

nodes.name: Metric uniformity
nodes.description: The uniformity on a metric space with entourage base {(x,y) : d(x,y) < epsilon} for epsilon > 0.

nodes.name: Equivalent norms on finite-dimensional spaces
nodes.description: On a finite-dimensional real vector space, all norms are equivalent, inducing the same topology.

nodes.name: Projective limit (inverse limit)
nodes.description: For a directed inverse system with connecting morphisms, the subspace of the product consisting of compatible threads.

nodes.name: Inductive limit (direct limit)
nodes.description: For a directed system with connecting morphisms, the quotient of the disjoint union identifying elements related by morphisms.

nodes.name: Solenoid
nodes.description: The projective limit of the inverse system ... -> S^1 ->^{xn} S^1, a compact connected abelian group not locally connected.

nodes.name: Profinite group
nodes.description: A topological group that is a projective limit of finite discrete groups; equivalently, compact totally disconnected Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Quasi-compact space
nodes.description: A topological space (not necessarily Hausdorff) in which every open cover has a finite subcover; Bourbaki reserves 'compact' for Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Finite intersection property characterization of compactness
nodes.description: A space is compact iff every collection of closed sets with the finite intersection property has nonempty intersection.

nodes.name: Continuous image of compact is compact
nodes.description: The continuous image of a compact space is compact.

nodes.name: Closed subsets of compact spaces are compact
nodes.description: Every closed subset of a compact space is compact; every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed.

nodes.name: Compact Hausdorff implies normal
nodes.description: Every compact Hausdorff space is normal (T4).

nodes.name: Continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff is homeomorphism
nodes.description: A continuous bijection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space is automatically a homeomorphism.

nodes.name: Proper map
nodes.description: A continuous map f : X -> Y such that preimages of compact sets are compact (equivalently, f x id_Z is closed for every Z).

nodes.name: Locally finite family
nodes.description: A family of subsets such that every point has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many members.

nodes.name: Refinement of a cover
nodes.description: A cover {V_j} refines {U_i} if every V_j is contained in some U_i.

nodes.name: Paracompactness of metrizable spaces (Stone's theorem)
nodes.description: Every metrizable space is paracompact; every open cover has a sigma-discrete open refinement.

nodes.name: Nowhere dense set
nodes.description: A set whose closure has empty interior.

nodes.name: Meager set (first category)
nodes.description: A countable union of nowhere dense sets; by Baire's theorem, a complete metric space is not meager in itself.

nodes.name: Characterization of semicontinuity via liminf/limsup
nodes.description: f is lower semicontinuous at x iff f(x) <= lim inf_{y->x} f(y); upper iff f(x) >= lim sup_{y->x} f(y).

nodes.name: Supremum of lower semicontinuous functions
nodes.description: The pointwise supremum of any family of lower semicontinuous functions is lower semicontinuous.

nodes.name: Paracompactness and partitions of unity
nodes.description: A Hausdorff space is paracompact iff every open cover admits a subordinate partition of unity.

nodes.name: Lindelof space
nodes.description: A topological space in which every open cover has a countable subcover.

nodes.name: Second-countable implies Lindelof
nodes.description: Every second-countable space is Lindelof, separable, and hereditarily Lindelof.

nodes.name: Compact-open topology
nodes.description: The topology on C(X,Y) generated by subbasic sets {f : f(K) subset U} where K compact and U open.

nodes.name: Topology of uniform convergence
nodes.description: The topology on function spaces defined by the uniformity: f and g are V-close if (f(x),g(x)) in V for all x.

nodes.name: Topology of compact convergence
nodes.description: The topology on C(X,Y) defined by uniform convergence on each compact subset of X.

nodes.name: Pointwise convergence topology
nodes.description: The topology on Y^X induced by the product topology; convergence means convergence at each point.

nodes.name: Evaluation map
nodes.description: The map ev : C(X,Y) x X -> Y defined by ev(f,x) = f(x); continuous when C(X,Y) has the compact-open topology and X is locally compact.

nodes.name: Exponential law for function spaces
nodes.description: For locally compact Hausdorff X, C(X x Y, Z) -> C(Y, C(X,Z)) by currying is a homeomorphism under compact-open topology.

nodes.name: Uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous
nodes.description: C(X,Y) is closed in Y^X under the topology of uniform convergence when Y is Hausdorff.

nodes.name: Completeness of function spaces
nodes.description: If Y is a complete uniform space, the space of bounded uniformly continuous functions X -> Y is complete under uniform convergence.

nodes.name: Filter generated by a base
nodes.description: The unique smallest filter containing a given filter base, consisting of all supersets of members of the base.

nodes.name: Finer and coarser topologies
